results.title: Enverge alternative: GPUwerk vs Enverge for DGX Spark rental
results.author: Samuel Seidel
highlights:
By Samuel Seidel · Published October 11, 2026 · 7 min read

Enverge and GPUwerk both rent a dedicated NVIDIA DGX Spark by the minute. Since Enverge raised its rate, GPUwerk is cheaper per running hour ($0.79 against $0.85). Enverge lists 4 TB of storage against 1 TB, and has a four-node tier. GPUwerk is in the Czech Republic under an EU operator with a published GDPR Article 28 DPA, and a stopped GPUwerk instance keeps its workspace at 75% of the rate, where Enverge bills until you delete the instance and its data. I run GPUwerk, so read this with that in mind. Every Enverge figure below comes from Enverge's own pages, checked on 9 November 2026 and linked at the end.

...

| | GPUwerk | Enverge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One Spark, running | $0.79/hour on demand. (advantage) | $0.85/hour on demand. The Spark page marks founder support "during beta". |
| Clusters | Two nodes at $1.79/hour (256 GB across two nodes, not one memory pool). No four-node option. | Two nodes at $1.90/hour, four nodes at $4.50/hour. Enverge's docs also say the 256 GB is two 128 GB pools, not one address space. |
| Billing | Per minute from prepaid credit. Account plus a $20 minimum top-up. | Metered in minutes from create to delete, "rounded up per billing bucket", invoiced daily to a card on file. |
| Pausing | Stop keeps the machine and the workspace at 75% of the rate ($0.59/hour). Terminate ends billing and deletes the workspace. (advantage) | "Stopping does not pause billing." Charges end only when you delete the instance, and deleting destroys its data. |
| Storage | 1 TB NVMe. GPUwerk keeps no copy of the workspace, so backups are yours. | 4 TB NVMe, listed as "Ephemeral or Persistent" on the Spark page. The terms say storage is ephemeral, with no backups or snapshots. (advantage) |
| Fixed-term booking | Monthly reservations from 1 to 24 months, up to 35% off. A 12-month term is $432.53 a month. | Reservations of 1 to 5 consecutive days at a flat $16.80 a day, paid up front. Nothing longer. |
| When nothing is free | The console shows live availability, and you can join a waitlist. | A free first-in, first-out queue. The docs say a wait "can run from hours to days" under heavy demand. |
| Inside the instance | Root in your own container on a dedicated Spark. On many Sparks it runs systemd and its own Docker daemon (docker run --gpus all works); others run a plain container without Docker, and you can't choose which. Browser terminal or SSH with your own key. | A container sandbox on dedicated, single-tenant hardware. Docker is preinstalled inside it and can reach the GPU with the NVIDIA runtime. SSH through Enverge's relay. |
| Where the machine is | Czech Republic (EU-Central) on GPUwerk's own tiers. The Partner tier runs at an independent partner's premises, in an EU or EEA country unless you choose a location outside it. You may use any data on it. (advantage) | The homepage names three fleet regions: us-west-1 (US), br-east-1 (Brazil) and eu-south-1 (Greece). No page I read says which region the Sparks are in. Customer traffic goes through a relay in Amsterdam. |
| Contract and data protection | PRINT IT! SE, Prague. A published GDPR Article 28 DPA. (advantage) | Enverge Corp, Delaware, under Delaware law. The terms list GDPR rights you can exercise by email. They do not mention a data processing agreement. |
| SLA | None published. | None. The terms say there is no SLA or uptime guarantee. |
| Other hardware | RTX 5090 (32 GB) at $0.89/hour; single GPUs from the L4 to the B300 at $0.49 to $6.49/hour, and whole 8-GPU servers from $21.52/hour. See the GPU catalog. | RTX Pro 6000 at $1.95/hour and Mac Studio M5 Ultra at $2.50; H100 at $4, H200 at $5.50 and B300 at $9.50 on request. |

Checked 2026-11-09. Highlighted cells mark the stronger option for that row. Enverge sources are listed at the end of this page. GPUwerk figures come from GPUwerk's published pricing, the tenant environment page and the DPA.

...

On running time alone GPUwerk is now cheaper. The $0.06 an hour is $2.40 over a 40-hour week of use ($31.60 at GPUwerk, $34.00 at Enverge) and $9.60 over 160 hours ($126.40 against $136.00). Over a full month of 730 hours, Enverge's homepage puts a Spark at about $621, against $576.70 at GPUwerk's on-demand rate, and a 12-month GPUwerk term is $432.53 a month.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU list prices up to 21% while H100 spot sits at $0.79 - CTOL Digital Solutions
highlights:
### What changed in the price list

The Nebius pricing documentation dates two changes. The first took effect on 1 October, when on demand prices per GPU hour rose for four chips. Reuters reported on 17 September that Nebius had announced it, its second price rise in three months.

- B300 went from $7.85 to $9.50, up 21.0 percent, the largest rise.
- B200 went from $7.15 to $8.50, up 18.9 percent.
- H200 went from $4.50 to $5.40, up 20.0 percent.
- H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50, up 16.9 percent, the smallest rise of the four.

The RTX PRO 6000 stayed at $1.80, so the rise did not reach every GPU.

The second change came on 8 October. The preemptible tier, which rents interruptible capacity at a discount, stopped using fixed prices. It moved to dynamic spot pricing that can change every 15 minutes.

One rule in the documentation matters most. The highest spot price is always one cent below the current on demand rate, so the new list price is a ceiling. The floor is $0.79 or $0.99 depending on the chip. The posted price rise matters to a spot buyer only when the market pushes against that ceiling.

results.title: Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23 | S&P Global
highlights:
Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23 | S&P Global 

 November 05, 2026

# Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23

Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, will launch US GPU Compute prices, effective Nov. 23, 2026.

Daily on-demand and interruptible prices will cover four NVIDIA chips: the NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips. Prices will be published in US dollars per GPU-hour and US dollars per million tokens of output, based on prices and availability at 1:30 pm CT.

...

The assessments reflect the market value of available NVIDIA GPU compute capacity delivered through qualifying virtualized infrastructure services in the US by providers and marketplaces. The new assessments will capture an evolving segment of the compute market, where growing availability of dedicated GPU capacity and increasingly standardized service offerings have supported greater price transparency. The assessments will provide standardized price references for accessing GPU compute capacity in the US, adding further granularity to Platts coverage of the infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence workloads.

METHODOLOGY

Each GPU price will be a simple average of the prices of available GPUs for each chip and service type. Platts will review the prices for outliers and will automatically exclude any prices greater than 2 median absolute deviations from the median.

...

results.title: Nebius and CoreWeave Lift Nvidia GPU Prices by Up to 21% – Trades Prophet
highlights:
Nvidia rental prices are rising even for last-generation H100s. Nebius has posted an October 1, 2026 on-demand card that lifts selected Nvidia GPU-hour rates by 16.9% to 21.0%. CoreWeave said on September 17 that it is still signing compute at higher prices, including short contracts at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue. A landlord can charge more for a chip it does not make only while that chip stays scarce. That is the signal behind Nvidia, and it is the opposite of a capacity glut.

Nebius’s price page, checked on October 2, still prints two columns. On-demand H100 is $3.85 per GPU-hour. The column marked effective October 1 is $4.50. The same split runs through the H200, the B200, and the B300. Reuters reported on September 17 that this was the second pay-as-you-go increase in about three months, with selected Nvidia GPU rates up 17% to 21%. The card on nebius.com/prices matches that range. It does not show every customer already paying the new rate.

...

Four Nvidia rows have a public before and after. GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 racks are still “contact us” in both columns. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. L40S “from” rates do not move. The hike lands on the accelerators customers are queued for.

| Nvidia GPU | Prior on-demand column | Announced October 1 card | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HGX H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | +$0.65, or 16.9% |
| HGX H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | +$0.90, or 20.0% |
| HGX B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | +$1.35, or 18.9% |
| HGX B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | +$1.65, or 21.0% |

...

October 2 is after the effective date, and the page still shows both numbers. The left-hand label is still “On-demand, GPU-hour.” The right-hand label is “GPU-hour (Effective October 1, 2026).” A customer cannot tell, from the page alone, which figure the console will bill.

GPU Finder’s Nebius page, with availability checked at 06:23 UTC on October 2, still listed one-GPU on-demand rates of $3.85 for the H100, $7.15 for the B200, and $7.85 for the B300. Those are the old column. The same check already showed the H200 at $5.40, the new column, with a spot print of $2.45 beside it. The H100 spot print on that row was $2.15. The tracker has not frozen. It has moved one of the four headline GPUs and left the other three on the pre-October number. Treating the whole book as repriced at midnight on October 1 would be tidier, and it would be wrong.

results.title: Verda raises prices again — all nine GPUs up about 1%, the eighth rise since Oct 23 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Verda's own pricing page today, Nov 2, 2026, against the figures read there on Nov 1: every GPU in Verda's range rose by about 1% — GB300, B300, B200, H200, H100, both A100s, the RTX PRO 6000 and the L40S. After two flat checks, the October rise run has resumed.

Image: Verda via verda.com

What changed, read on verda.com/pricing on Nov 2, 2026 (unrounded page figures in brackets): GB300 $13.05 → $13.18 [$13.18], B300 $11.35 → $11.46 [$11.46], B200 $8.87 → $8.96 [$8.958], H200 $6.25 → $6.31 [$6.313], H100 SXM $4.79 → $4.84 [$4.841], A100 80GB $2.25 → $2.27 [$2.270], A100 40GB $1.61 → $1.63 [$1.625], RTX PRO 6000 $2.65 → $2.67 [$2.671] and L40S $1.90 → $1.92 [$1.920]. Each move is within a cent of +1.0% — a uniform list adjustment, not one card repricing.

...

What it costs: Verda holds the board's Best offer on only two cards — the GB300 and the A100 40GB — and both rose today, so those two best offers rose with it. Everywhere else the cheapest verified offers are other providers' and none moved: the board's H100 SXM best is still TensorDock at $2.25 an hour (at an 8-GPU minimum) and its B200 best is still RunPod Community at $5.98. If you rent at Verda around the clock, today's rise adds about $95 a month per GB300, $65 per B200 and $35 per H100 on a 730-hour month — small per hour, real per fleet.
